messages:
maya: FYI link-checker exploded on the staging build: lots of anchor mismatches after the mkdocs -> docusaurus migration. Examples include headings with emoji and CJK characters getting different slugs. ryan: I saw that. `# デプロイ手順` becomes `#%E3%83%87%E3%83%97%E3%83%AD%E3%82%A4%E3%81%A6%E9%A0%86` in some places and `#デプロイ手順` in others. Anchor normalization differs between the two generators. jess: Repro steps? I can try locally. maya: Run `yarn workspace site build && npx linkinator ./build -r` - output shows 23 fragment mismatches. Sample: `/docs/how-to/upgrade#デプロイ手順` -> 404 but page has `

` (sigh). kyle: The core issue: mkdocs-slugify kept japanese characters in the slug while Docusaurus runs a different slugifier that transliterates or drops certain unicode categories. We need a deterministic postprocessor that rewrites internal fragment links to the Docusaurus-generated slug style. ryan: Agree. Two approaches: 1) normalize headings to ascii-friendly slugs (in frontmatter or an explicit `id:` in markdown) OR 2) remap links to the generated anchor after build (walk built HTML and rewrite links). Option 1 is better for long-term docs hygiene. jess: Can we automate adding `id:`? For headings where the slug changed we could insert an HTML anchor like `` or use `{#custom-slug}` syntax if supported. But touching many files is scary. maya: I prototyped a script: parse each markdown heading, compute docusaurus slug using the same algorithm (node slugger lib), and if original link points to different slug, add a HTML shortlink comment above heading: ``. Then a small client-side JS plugin can read these and add aliases. kyle: clever, but client-side JS adds runtime work. I'd prefer compile-time reconciliation. Maybe generate a redirects map that maps old fragment urls to new ones and feed to the link-checker/redirect middleware. ryan: Also noticed code fences lost language tags when they were `yaml+jinja` style and MkDocs allowed them; Docusaurus strips `+` variants. That broke several SDK snippets that rely on syntax highlighting for `dockerfile` vs `bash`. jess: For code fences we can normalize languages to Docusaurus supported list. Plan: small lint rule that flags nonstandard fence languages and an autofix that replaces `yaml+jinja` -> `jinja` or `yaml` depending on detection. maya: Proposed immediate next steps: 1) Run a full linkinator pass and emit a report of mismatched fragments (already done). 2) Add a script to compute Docusaurus slugs for headings and produce a JSON map: `{oldFragment: newFragment}`. 3) Apply an automated PR that updates internal markdown links (only inside docs/, not external links) using the map. 4) Add a linter rule to reject new markdown with ambiguous fence languages. kyle: I'll take step 2 and 3 as a pair. Using `@docusaurus/utils` slugger gives consistent slugs. Then a small node script can `glob docs/**/*.md` and replace link hrefs where needed. jess: I'll add the markdownlint rule and autofix for codefences. I'll also add tests to the docs CI that run these linters. maya: docs-bot: can you open a tracking ticket? doc-bot: Created ticket DOCS-1428 and opened PR `docs: reconcile anchors + normalize codefences (kyle/jess)` — CI pending. lint-bot: Lint report on PR: flagged 12 files with codefence language issues and 18 link replacements to perform. ryan: Small caution: don't touch external links or anchor links that intentionally point to third-party anchors. Limit replacements to links that start with `/docs/` or relative paths. kyle: Good call. I'll scope replace to links matching `^\/?docs\/|^\.\.` and add a dry-run mode. jess: After PR merge, let's run a full e2e on staging and then re-run the marketing QA checklist. maya: Sounds good. If anyone hits weird unicode oddities, ping me. I'll coordinate with localization to ensure translators avoid embedding emoji in headings. kyle: Pushed draft PR with dry-run output in the PR description. PTAL. doc-bot: PR build: link-check step passed in dry-run. Waiting for reviewers. jess: Reviewed and applied autofix suggestions for code fences. Added changelog entry. maya: Thanks all — merging once CI passes. We'll monitor any residual linkcheck flaps post-deploy. Close thread when green.
